It decreases, because more protons pull the same shells closer
It holds steady, because the number of shells stays the same
S.w: Across a period, electrons are added to the same outer shell while the nuclear charge (number of protons) increases. The stronger pull draws the electron cloud inward, so atomic radius decreases from left to right.

n.0: More electrons are added, but they go into the same shell while the growing nuclear charge pulls them in, so radius shrinks.
n.1: A new shell is added when moving down a group (or starting a new period), not across a period.
n.3: The shell count is unchanged, but the rising number of protons still pulls the shells closer, so radius does change.

S.q: During a lumbar puncture, a needle is inserted between two lumbar vertebrae into the fluid-filled space of the vertebral canal. Which body cavity, and its larger division, does this space belong to?
o: The cranial cavity, part of the ventral cavity
The mediastinum, part of the thoracic cavity
The pelvic cavity, part of the ventral cavity
The vertebral cavity, part of the dorsal cavity
S.w: The spinal cord lies in the vertebral (spinal) cavity. Together with the cranial cavity, it forms the dorsal body cavity, protected by bone and meninges.

n.0: The cranial cavity holds the brain, and it belongs to the dorsal cavity, not the ventral cavity.
n.1: The mediastinum is in the ventral thoracic cavity and holds the heart, trachea and esophagus, not the spinal cord.
n.2: The pelvic cavity holds the bladder, rectum and reproductive organs; the spinal cord lies in the dorsal cavity.

S.q: Aldosterone from the adrenal cortex acts on the distal convoluted tubule and collecting duct. What is its effect on the handling of sodium and potassium?
o: Water is reabsorbed while sodium is unchanged
Sodium is reabsorbed and potassium is secreted
Sodium and potassium are both reabsorbed
Potassium is reabsorbed and sodium is secreted
S.w: Aldosterone makes the DCT and collecting duct reabsorb sodium (water follows) and secrete potassium, raising blood volume and blood pressure.

n.0: Water reabsorption with no change in sodium describes ADH, not aldosterone.
n.2: Aldosterone increases potassium secretion into the urine, not potassium reabsorption.
n.3: This reverses aldosterone's action, a common trap: it keeps sodium and excretes potassium.

S.q: Shortly after a meal high in fat, cells of the duodenum release a hormone that makes the gallbladder contract. Which hormone is this, and what other effect does it have?
o: Secretin; it also triggers pancreatic bicarbonate release
Glucagon; it also triggers glycogen breakdown
Gastrin; it also triggers gastric acid secretion
Cholecystokinin; it also triggers pancreatic enzyme release
S.w: Cholecystokinin (CCK) from the duodenum makes the gallbladder contract to release bile and stimulates the pancreas to release its digestive enzymes.

n.0: Secretin does trigger bicarbonate release from the pancreas, but it is not the hormone that contracts the gallbladder.
n.1: Glucagon is a pancreatic islet hormone that raises blood glucose; it is not a duodenal hormone.
n.2: Gastrin comes from the stomach and stimulates acid secretion; it does not contract the gallbladder.

S.q: After a large meal, a person's liver and skeletal muscles store excess glucose as a highly branched polysaccharide. Which molecule is formed?
o: Glycogen
Starch
Cellulose
Chitin
S.w: Animals store glucose as glycogen in the liver and muscles. Starch is the plant storage form.

n.1: Starch is the storage polysaccharide of plants, not animals.
n.2: Cellulose is a structural polysaccharide in plant cell walls.
n.3: Chitin is a structural polysaccharide in fungal walls and insect exoskeletons.

S.q: A student is preparing a summary of what separates a scientific explanation from other kinds of claims. Which features make an explanation scientific? Select all that apply.
o: It is accepted because experts hold it.
It can be reproduced by other scientists.
It is testable and could be falsified.
It rests on many personal stories.
It is based on empirical evidence.
It is proven and closed to revision.
S.w: Scientific explanations rest on empirical evidence (observation and measurement), are testable and falsifiable, and are reproducible by others. They stay open to revision when new evidence appears.

n.0: Authority is not evidence; experts' claims must still be backed by data.
n.3: Personal stories are anecdotal evidence, which lacks controls and cannot establish cause.
n.5: Scientific explanations stay open to revision; evidence supports them but does not prove them.

S.q: Consider the gas-phase reaction 2 SO₂ + O₂ ⇌ 2 SO₃ at equilibrium. If the volume of the container is decreased, raising the pressure, which way will the equilibrium shift?
o: Toward SO₂ and O₂, the side with more moles of gas
Toward SO₃, the side with fewer moles of gas
Toward SO₂ and O₂, because pressure favors reactants
No shift, because pressure changes rates, not position
S.w: Increasing pressure shifts an equilibrium toward the side with fewer moles of gas, which reduces the pressure. The left side has 2 + 1 = 3 moles of gas and the right side has 2, so the shift is toward SO₃.

n.0: Shifting toward more gas molecules would raise the pressure further; the system shifts to reduce the stress.
n.2: Pressure does not favor reactants as a rule; it favors whichever side has fewer moles of gas.
n.3: Changing pressure by changing volume does shift an equilibrium when the two sides have different numbers of gas moles.

S.q: In a sealed flask, 10.0 g of baking soda reacts completely with 20.0 g of vinegar, producing carbon dioxide gas that stays inside the flask. What is the total mass of the flask's contents after the reaction?
o: Less than 30.0 g, because a gas has very little mass
Less than 30.0 g, because some mass is converted into energy
More than 30.0 g, because a new compound has formed
Exactly 30.0 g, because atoms are rearranged, not lost
S.w: The law of conservation of mass: atoms are rearranged in a reaction, not created or destroyed, so the total mass of the products equals the total mass of the reactants (10.0 g + 20.0 g = 30.0 g) in a closed system.

n.0: Gas does have mass; in a sealed flask the carbon dioxide is still counted. Mass would seem to drop only if the gas escaped from an open container.
n.1: In ordinary chemical reactions the mass change from energy release is far too small to measure; mass is conserved.
n.2: Forming a new compound rearranges the same atoms, so the total mass does not increase.

S.q: During elbow flexion, the biceps brachii pulls the radius toward the shoulder while its attachments on the scapula stay fixed. How is the attachment on the radius classified?
o: Origin, because it is on the bone that moves
Origin, because it is farther from the trunk
Insertion, because it is on the bone that moves
Insertion, because it is on the stationary bone
S.w: The origin is the attachment on the more stationary bone (here the scapula); the insertion is on the bone that moves (the radius). During contraction the insertion is pulled toward the origin.

n.0: The attachment on the moving bone is the insertion; the origin is on the more stationary bone.
n.1: Origin and insertion are defined by which bone moves, not by distance from the trunk; the moving radius carries the insertion.
n.3: The insertion is on the bone that moves; the stationary attachment is the origin.

S.q: A student is sorting bones into the axial and appendicular divisions of the skeleton. Which of the following bones belongs to the axial skeleton?
o: Hip bone (os coxae)
Clavicle
Hyoid
Scapula
S.w: The axial skeleton (80 bones) is the skull, hyoid, auditory ossicles, vertebral column and rib cage. The pectoral girdle (clavicle, scapula) and the pelvic girdle (hip bones) belong to the appendicular skeleton.

n.0: The hip bones form the pelvic girdle, which is appendicular even though it joins the sacrum.
n.1: The clavicle is part of the pectoral girdle, which belongs to the appendicular skeleton.
n.3: The scapula is part of the pectoral girdle, which belongs to the appendicular skeleton.

S.q: As Marisol walks from a dark theater into bright sunlight, her pupils shrink. Which structure of the eye changes the size of the pupil?
o: Lens
Ciliary muscle
Cornea
Iris
S.w: The pupil is the opening in the iris, and the iris controls its size to regulate how much light enters the eye.

n.0: The lens focuses light on the retina; it does not change the size of the pupil.
n.1: The ciliary muscles change the shape of the lens, not the size of the pupil.
n.2: The cornea is the clear front surface that light passes through first; it cannot change size.

S.q: A culture starts with one bacterial cell. It divides by binary fission every 20 minutes, and every new cell keeps dividing at that rate. Enter the number of cells after 2 hours as a whole number.

tr.7: Counted 1 cell plus 1 new cell per generation (1 + 6).
tr.12: Added 2 cells per generation (6 x 2), a linear doubling instead of exponential growth.

S.w: Step 1: 2 hours = 120 minutes, and 120 / 20 = 6 generations. Step 2: each generation doubles the population (exponential growth), so the count after n generations is 2^n = 2^6 = 64 cells (1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64).

S.q: A chemist needs an element whose chemical properties are most similar to those of sulfur (group 16, period 3). Which element should she choose, and why?
o: Chlorine, in the same period as sulfur
Phosphorus, with the nearest atomic mass
Selenium, in the same group as sulfur
Sodium, with the same number of shells
S.w: Elements in the same group have the same number of valence electrons, so they have similar chemical properties. Selenium is directly below sulfur in group 16; both have 6 valence electrons.

n.0: Elements in the same period have different numbers of valence electrons and different properties; chlorine has 7.
n.1: Similar atomic mass does not mean similar chemistry; phosphorus has 5 valence electrons.
n.3: Sharing the number of shells (the same period) does not give similar properties; sodium is a reactive metal with 1 valence electron.

S.q: After a vasectomy, a man's semen contains no sperm, yet its volume is only slightly reduced. Which explanation accounts for this?
o: Most of the fluid enters past the cut, from the seminal vesicles and prostate
Most of the fluid comes from the seminiferous tubules, which keep secreting
Most of the fluid is made in the epididymis, which lies past the cut
Most of the fluid comes from the bulbourethral glands, which drain into the ductus
S.w: Two steps. (1) A vasectomy cuts the ductus (vas) deferens, so sperm from the seminiferous tubules and epididymis cannot pass. (2) The seminal vesicles (about 60% of semen) join the tract at the ejaculatory duct, and the prostate surrounds the urethra; both lie downstream of the cut, so their fluid still makes up most of the semen.

n.1: The seminiferous tubules produce sperm and lie upstream of the cut, so nothing from them reaches the ejaculate.
n.2: The epididymis lies before the ductus deferens, upstream of the cut, and it matures and stores sperm rather than making most of the semen fluid.
n.3: The bulbourethral glands add a small amount of mucus, and they drain into the urethra, not the ductus deferens.

S.q: Carbon dioxide produced by working muscle must be carried to the lungs. In which form is most of this carbon dioxide transported in the blood?
o: Bound to hemoglobin as carbaminohemoglobin
Bound to the iron atoms of heme groups
Dissolved as carbon dioxide gas in plasma
As bicarbonate ions in the plasma
S.w: About 70% of CO₂ is carried as bicarbonate (HCO₃⁻), formed inside red blood cells by carbonic anhydrase and then moved into the plasma. About 20-23% rides on hemoglobin and 7-10% is dissolved.

n.0: Carbaminohemoglobin carries only about a fifth of the CO₂, not most of it.
n.1: Iron in heme binds oxygen; CO₂ that binds hemoglobin attaches to the globin protein, and it is still the minority route.
n.2: Only about 7-10% of CO₂ is carried dissolved in plasma.

S.q: A lab manual describes cell walls built from cellulose, chitin and peptidoglycan. Which pairing of wall material and cell is correct?
o: Cellulose in the wall of a bacterial cell
Cellulose in the wall of a yeast cell
Peptidoglycan in the wall of a plant cell
Chitin in the wall of a mold cell
S.w: Molds and yeasts are fungi, and fungal cell walls are made of chitin. Plant walls are cellulose and bacterial walls are peptidoglycan.

n.0: Bacterial walls are made of peptidoglycan, not cellulose.
n.1: Yeast is a fungus, so its wall contains chitin rather than the cellulose found in plants.
n.2: Plant cell walls are made of cellulose. Peptidoglycan is the bacterial wall material.

S.q: Which events occur during the luteal phase of a 28-day cycle in which pregnancy does not occur? Select all that apply.
o: An LH surge triggers rupture of the dominant follicle.
The corpus luteum degenerates and progesterone falls.
FSH stimulates the growth of a dominant follicle.
The corpus luteum secretes progesterone.
The endometrium is in its secretory phase.
The functional layer of the endometrium is shed.
S.w: The luteal phase (about days 15 to 28) follows ovulation: the corpus luteum secretes progesterone, the endometrium is secretory, and with no embryo making hCG the corpus luteum degenerates late in the phase, so progesterone falls.

n.0: The LH surge and follicle rupture occur at ovulation, about day 14, which ends the follicular phase.
n.2: FSH-driven growth of the dominant follicle happens in the follicular phase, before ovulation.
n.5: Shedding of the functional layer is the menstrual phase (days 1 to 5), which follows the fall in progesterone.

S.q: Digestion includes both mechanical and chemical processes. Which pairing of a digestive process with its type of digestion is correct?
o: Segmentation mixing chyme in the small intestine: mechanical
Lactase splitting lactose at the brush border: mechanical
Churning of food by the stomach's muscle layers: chemical
Salivary amylase breaking starch into maltose: mechanical
S.w: Mechanical digestion physically breaks up and mixes food: chewing, stomach churning and segmentation in the small intestine. Enzymes breaking chemical bonds is chemical digestion.

n.1: Lactase is an enzyme that hydrolyzes lactose into glucose and galactose, so this is chemical digestion.
n.2: Churning physically breaks up and mixes food without breaking chemical bonds, so it is mechanical digestion.
n.3: Salivary amylase is an enzyme that breaks chemical bonds in starch, so this is chemical digestion.

S.q: Pepsin digests protein in the stomach, where the pH is about 2. If pepsin passes into the small intestine, where the pH is about 8, what will most likely happen to its activity?
o: It will fall, since pH 8 is far from pepsin's optimum.
It will stay the same, since pH does not affect enzymes.
It will rise, since trypsin activates pepsin at pH 8.
It will rise, since enzymes work faster in basic solutions.
S.w: Each enzyme has an optimum pH. Pepsin works best near pH 2, so at pH 8 its shape changes and activity falls. Trypsin, with an optimum near pH 8, works in the small intestine.

n.1: pH strongly affects enzyme shape and activity.
n.2: Trypsin is a separate protein-digesting enzyme with its own optimum; it does not boost pepsin.
n.3: Enzymes do not all work faster in basic conditions; each has its own optimum, and pepsin's is acidic.

S.q: In a fetus, the umbilical vein carries blood from the placenta to the fetus. Based on how veins are defined, which statement is correct?
o: It carries deoxygenated blood toward the fetal heart
It carries oxygenated blood toward the fetal heart
It carries oxygenated blood away from the fetal heart
It carries deoxygenated blood away from the fetal heart
S.w: Step 1: a vein carries blood toward the heart. Step 2: blood leaving the placenta has picked up oxygen, so the umbilical vein carries oxygenated blood toward the fetal heart (the umbilical arteries carry deoxygenated blood away).

n.0: Blood coming from the placenta has just been oxygenated there.
n.2: Carrying blood away from the heart would make it an artery.
n.3: This describes the umbilical arteries, which return deoxygenated blood to the placenta.

S.q: During exercise, select the structure that cools the body by releasing a watery secretion through a pore onto the skin surface.
S.w: Eccrine sweat glands are coiled glands deep in the dermis and hypodermis whose ducts open through pores on the skin surface. Their watery sweat evaporates and carries heat away, which makes them the main thermoregulatory glands.

n.sebaceous: Sebaceous glands secrete oily sebum, usually into hair follicles, to lubricate skin and hair. Sebum does not cool the body.
n.vessel: Dilation of dermal blood vessels also releases heat, by bringing warm blood near the surface, but vessels secrete nothing onto the skin.
n.follicle: Hair follicles produce hair. Apocrine glands empty into them, but the watery cooling secretion reaches the surface through its own pores.
n.receptor: The lamellated corpuscle is a sensory receptor for deep pressure and vibration. It secretes nothing.

S.q: In a trial of a blood-pressure drug, neither the patients nor the nurses who take the readings know which patients receive the drug and which receive a placebo. Which term describes this design feature?
o: Observational study
Double-blind
Random sampling
Single-blind
S.w: In a double-blind study, neither the subjects nor the researchers who measure outcomes know group assignments, which reduces bias from both expectations.

n.0: An observational study assigns no treatment; this trial gives a drug or placebo.
n.2: Random sampling is how participants are chosen so the sample represents the population; it does not hide group assignments.
n.3: Single-blind means the subjects do not know their group, but the researchers do.

S.q: Cardiac muscle and skeletal muscle differ in many ways. Which features do these two muscle types share? Select all that apply.
o: Actin and myosin organized into sarcomeres
Spindle-shaped cells with one nucleus
Long cylindrical cells with many nuclei
Striated appearance under a microscope
Cells joined by intercalated discs
Voluntary control by somatic motor neurons
S.w: Both are striated because their actin and myosin are arranged in repeating sarcomeres. Skeletal muscle is voluntary, with long multinucleated fibers; cardiac muscle is involuntary, with branched cells that usually have one nucleus and are joined by intercalated discs.

n.1: Spindle-shaped cells with one nucleus describe smooth muscle, not either of these types.
n.2: Long multinucleated cells are skeletal fibers; cardiac cells are branched and usually have one nucleus.
n.4: Intercalated discs are found in cardiac muscle and are absent from skeletal muscle.
n.5: Voluntary somatic control belongs to skeletal muscle; cardiac muscle is involuntary and autorhythmic.

S.q: An adult has burns covering the entire right arm and the entire front of the trunk. Using the adult rule of nines, what percentage of total body surface area is burned? Enter a whole number.

tr.18: counting the front of the trunk as 9%, like an arm (9 + 9)
tr.36: counting the arm as 18%, the value for a leg (18 + 18)
tr.45: adding the back of the trunk as well (9 + 18 + 18)

S.w: Adult rule of nines: each arm is 9% and the front of the trunk is 18%. 9 + 18 = 27%.

S.q: A nurse pours 30 mL of cough syrup from a tall, narrow bottle into a wide, shallow dosing cup. The syrup takes the shape of the cup but still measures 30 mL. Which description of the syrup's particles explains this behavior?
o: They are squeezed by the cup walls into the new shape
They are far apart and move freely to fill any container
They stay close together but can slide past one another
They vibrate in fixed positions that hold a set volume
S.w: Liquids have a definite volume but no definite shape. Their particles stay close together (so the volume stays 30 mL) but can slide past one another (so the syrup flows into the shape of the cup).

n.0: Liquids are nearly incompressible; the volume stays 30 mL, so the particles are not being pushed closer together.
n.1: Particles that are far apart and move freely describe a gas, which would spread to fill the whole container instead of keeping 30 mL.
n.3: Particles vibrating in fixed positions describe a solid, which keeps its own shape instead of taking the shape of the cup.

S.q: A nursing student documents a healing wound on day 3. Which of her notes records quantitative data?
o: The wound measures 2.4 cm in length.
The patient describes the pain as sharp.
The dressing has a faint sour odor.
The wound edges look pink and dry.
S.w: Quantitative data are numbers with units, such as a length of 2.4 cm. Descriptions of color, odor or pain quality are qualitative.

n.1: A word describing pain quality is qualitative; a 0 to 10 pain score would be quantitative.
n.2: An odor description is qualitative.
n.3: Color and texture are descriptions, which makes them qualitative data.

S.q: A high school wrestler develops a red, ring-shaped, scaly rash and is diagnosed with tinea corporis (ringworm). Which type of medication is appropriate for this infection?
o: An antiviral
An antibiotic for bacteria
An antihelminthic for worms
An antifungal
S.w: Despite its name, ringworm (tinea) is a fungal skin infection, so it is treated with an antifungal.

n.0: Antivirals target viruses; tinea is caused by a fungus.
n.1: Antibiotics target bacteria; tinea is caused by a fungus.
n.2: Ringworm is not caused by a worm; the name comes from the ring-shaped rash.

S.q: A student dips strips of red and blue litmus paper into a household cleaner. The red strip turns blue, and the blue strip stays blue. What does this result show about the cleaner?
o: It is a base, with a pH below 7
It is an acid, with a pH below 7
It is a base, with a pH above 7
It is neutral, with a pH of 7
S.w: Bases turn red litmus blue; acids turn blue litmus red. A red strip turning blue identifies a base, and bases have a pH above 7.

n.0: It is a base, but a pH below 7 describes an acid; bases have a pH above 7.
n.1: An acid would turn the blue strip red and leave the red strip unchanged, which is the opposite of what was seen.
n.3: A neutral solution would not change the color of either litmus strip.

S.q: A father with type A blood (genotype IAi) and a mother with type B blood (genotype IBi) are expecting a child. Which blood types are possible for the child?
o: A and B, but not AB or O
A, B and AB, but not O
AB and O, but not A or B
A, B, AB and O
S.w: IAi x IBi gives IAIB (AB), IAi (A), IBi (B) and ii (O), each with a probability of 1/4.

n.0: This leaves out IAIB (AB) and ii (O), which are both possible because each parent can pass on either allele.
n.1: This leaves out type O; each parent carries i, so an ii child is possible.
n.2: This leaves out type A (IAi) and type B (IBi), which are also possible.

S.q: During protein synthesis, one type of RNA carries a specific amino acid and has a three-base anticodon. Which type of RNA is this?
o: Messenger RNA
Transfer RNA
Ribosomal RNA
Primer RNA
S.w: Transfer RNA (tRNA) carries a specific amino acid and has an anticodon that pairs with the matching mRNA codon at the ribosome.

n.0: mRNA carries the codons copied from DNA. It does not carry amino acids, and the anticodon is on tRNA.
n.2: rRNA is the structural and catalytic part of ribosomes; it does not carry amino acids or anticodons.
n.3: Primer RNA is the short strand primase lays down to start DNA replication; it carries no amino acid.

S.q: Oxygen gas can be squeezed into a small tank for a patient's portable supply, but liquid water barely changes volume even under great pressure. What explains this difference?
o: Gas particles move slowly, so they can be packed together
Gas particles attract one another more strongly than liquids
Gas particles are smaller than the particles of a liquid
Gas particles are far apart with much empty space between them
S.w: According to kinetic molecular theory, gas particles are far apart compared with their size, so there is a lot of empty space that can be reduced by pressure. Liquid particles are already close together.

n.0: Gas particles move fast, not slowly; they have the highest kinetic energy of the three common states.
n.1: Attractions between gas particles are weaker, not stronger, than in a liquid; a gas compresses because of the empty space between its particles.
n.2: Compressibility depends on the space between particles, not their size; water molecules are similar in size to oxygen molecules.

S.q: In pea plants, round seeds (R) are dominant over wrinkled (r) and yellow (Y) over green (y), on different chromosomes. If RrYy x RrYy produces 160 offspring, how many are expected to be round and yellow? Enter a whole number.
S.w: Step 1: a dihybrid cross gives a 9 : 3 : 3 : 1 phenotype ratio, so 9/16 show both dominant traits. Step 2: 160 x 9/16 = 90.

S.q: The coding region of an mRNA, from the start codon AUG through the stop codon, is 450 nucleotides long. How many amino acids will the resulting polypeptide contain? Enter a whole number.

tr.150: counted the stop codon as an amino acid
tr.450: assumed one nucleotide per amino acid

S.w: Step 1: each codon is 3 nucleotides, so 450 / 3 = 150 codons. Step 2: the last codon is a stop codon, which codes for no amino acid, so 150 - 1 = 149 amino acids.

S.q: A class measures an enzyme's activity at three temperatures. Data: 20 °C, 12 units; 30 °C, 24 units; 40 °C, 36 units. Which estimate of the activity at 35 °C is best supported by the data?
o: About 36 units
About 48 units
About 30 units
About 24 units
S.w: Activity rises 12 units for every 10 °C across the tested range, so halfway between 30 °C and 40 °C it should be about halfway between 24 and 36: about 30 units. Estimating between measured points (interpolation) is reliable.

n.0: 36 units is the measured value at 40 °C; 35 °C is only halfway there.
n.1: 48 units would follow the trend to 50 °C, beyond the range tested, not 35 °C.
n.3: 24 units is the measured value at 30 °C; the trend predicts a higher value at 35 °C.

S.q: The atrioventricular valve with three cusps opens, and blood moves from one chamber into another. Which chamber is receiving the blood?
o: Left ventricle
Right atrium
Pulmonary trunk
Right ventricle
S.w: Step 1: the AV valve with three cusps is the tricuspid valve, on the right side. Step 2: AV valves let blood pass from atrium to ventricle, so the right ventricle is receiving blood from the right atrium.

n.0: The left ventricle receives blood through the mitral (bicuspid) valve, which has two cusps.
n.1: The right atrium is the chamber sending blood through the tricuspid valve, not receiving it.
n.2: The pulmonary trunk receives blood through the pulmonary semilunar valve, not an AV valve.

S.q: A student checks a worksheet in which every value should be written in correct scientific notation. Which values are written correctly? Select all that apply.
S.w: Scientific notation is a × 10ⁿ with 1 <= a < 10. The coefficients 4.07, 1.0 and 9.99 all fall in that range; a negative exponent is allowed.

n.0: The coefficient 12.5 is 10 or greater; written correctly it is 1.25 × 10⁵.
n.1: A coefficient of 10 is not less than 10; written correctly it is 1 × 10³.
n.4: The coefficient 0.75 is less than 1; written correctly it is 7.5 × 10⁻⁴.

S.q: Three trials of a student's experiment all show that bean seeds soaked overnight sprout faster than dry bean seeds, as her hypothesis predicted. Which conclusion is worded correctly?
o: The data support the hypothesis, which is now a scientific theory.
The data prove the hypothesis for the bean seeds tested.
The data support the hypothesis for seeds of all plant species.
The data support the hypothesis for the bean seeds tested.
S.w: Data support or fail to support a hypothesis; they do not prove it. A sound conclusion also stays within what was tested (bean seeds), and one small experiment does not create a theory.

n.0: A theory is a broad explanation tested many times by many scientists; one student's three trials do not turn a hypothesis into a theory.
n.1: Data support a hypothesis but never prove it; a later replicated result could still contradict it, even for bean seeds.
n.2: Only bean seeds were tested, so extending the result to every plant species generalizes beyond the population studied.

S.q: A student is classifying four compounds by bond type. Which of these compounds is held together by covalent bonds?
o: Carbon dioxide (CO₂)
Potassium bromide (KBr)
Magnesium oxide (MgO)
Calcium chloride (CaCl₂)
S.w: Covalent bonds form when nonmetal atoms share electron pairs. Carbon and oxygen are both nonmetals, so CO₂ is a covalent (molecular) compound.

n.1: Potassium is a metal, so potassium bromide is ionic (K+ and Br⁻).
n.2: Magnesium is a metal and oxygen is a nonmetal, so MgO is ionic (Mg²⁺ and O²⁻).
n.3: Calcium is a metal, so calcium chloride is ionic (Ca²⁺ and two Cl⁻).

S.q: During weeks of ongoing stress before final exams, which hormone sustains Mei's long-term stress response by raising blood glucose and suppressing inflammation?
o: Cortisol from the adrenal cortex
Cortisol from the adrenal medulla
Epinephrine from the adrenal medulla
Aldosterone from the adrenal cortex
S.w: Cortisol, a glucocorticoid from the adrenal cortex, drives the long-term stress response: it raises blood glucose by gluconeogenesis, is anti-inflammatory and suppresses immunity.

n.1: Cortisol is the right hormone, but it comes from the adrenal cortex, not the medulla.
n.2: Epinephrine from the adrenal medulla drives the short-term, fight-or-flight response, not weeks of sustained stress.
n.3: Aldosterone from the adrenal cortex controls Na⁺ and K⁺ and blood volume, not glucose or inflammation.

S.q: A biology class is planning an investigation on pea plants and light. Which statement is written as a testable scientific hypothesis?
o: Pea plants should be given as many hours of light as a grower can provide.
Pea plants grown under bright light are more attractive than shaded ones.
Do pea plants grow taller when they receive more hours of light each day?
If pea plants get 8 hours of light daily instead of 4, they will grow taller.
S.w: A hypothesis is a testable, tentative prediction, often in "If ... then ..." form. Plant height can be measured under two light conditions, so this statement can be supported or refuted by data.

n.0: This is a recommendation about what growers should do, not a prediction that can be tested.
n.1: "More attractive" is an opinion that cannot be measured objectively, so it is not testable.
n.2: This is the research question; a hypothesis is a statement that predicts an answer.

S.q: Which ribs are called floating ribs because they have no anterior attachment to the sternum, either directly or through costal cartilage?
o: Ribs 8 through 12
Ribs 11 and 12
Ribs 1 through 7
Ribs 8 through 10
S.w: Ribs 1 to 7 are true ribs, each with its own costal cartilage to the sternum. Ribs 8 to 12 are false ribs: 8 to 10 attach through the cartilage of rib 7, and 11 and 12 are floating ribs with no anterior attachment.

n.0: Ribs 8 to 12 are the false ribs; within that group, 8 to 10 still attach indirectly, so they do not float.
n.2: Ribs 1 to 7 are true ribs that attach directly to the sternum by their own costal cartilage.
n.3: Ribs 8 to 10 are false ribs that reach the sternum indirectly through rib 7's costal cartilage.

S.q: Stirring a cup of iced tea makes the added sugar dissolve faster. Which statement correctly describes what stirring changes?
o: The temperature of the tea, which raises the solubility
The solubility of sugar, so more sugar can dissolve in total
The speed of dissolving, but not the solubility of sugar
Both the solubility of sugar and the speed of dissolving
S.w: Stirring brings fresh solvent into contact with the solute, increasing the rate of dissolving. Solubility, the maximum amount that can dissolve, depends on temperature (and pressure for gases), not on stirring.

n.0: Stirring does not noticeably change the temperature of the tea, so it does not change solubility.
n.1: Stirring affects how fast sugar dissolves, not the total amount that can dissolve.
n.3: Stirring changes the rate only; solubility at a given temperature is fixed.

S.q: Tendons attach skeletal muscles to bones and must resist strong pulling forces in one direction. Which tissue forms tendons?
o: Dense irregular connective tissue
Loose areolar connective tissue
Dense regular connective tissue
Skeletal muscle tissue
S.w: Tendons and ligaments are dense regular connective tissue: tightly packed collagen fibers run parallel to one another, resisting strong pull in one direction.

n.0: Dense irregular connective tissue has collagen fibers running in many directions, suited to pull from several directions (as in the dermis), not the parallel fibers of a tendon.
n.1: Areolar tissue is loose connective tissue with a loose, open arrangement of fibers; it does not withstand strong one-direction pull.
n.3: Skeletal muscle generates the pull; the tendon that transmits it to bone is connective tissue.

S.q: A graduated cylinder holds 42.0 mL of water. A student lowers a small stone into it, and the level rises to 57.5 mL. A balance shows the stone's mass is 31.0 g. What is the density of the stone?
o: 2.0 g/mL
S.w: Step 1: volume by water displacement = final level - initial level = 57.5 mL - 42.0 mL = 15.5 mL. Step 2: density = mass / volume = 31.0 g / 15.5 mL = 2.0 g/mL.

n.0: This divides volume by mass (15.5 / 31.0); density is mass divided by volume.
n.1: This divides the mass by the final water level (31.0 / 57.5) instead of by the displaced volume.
n.2: This divides the mass by the starting water level (31.0 / 42.0) instead of by the change in level.

S.q: Spinning rapidly on an office chair leaves Tomás dizzy. Which structures contain the receptors that detect the rotation of his head?
o: Auditory (Eustachian) tube
Cochlea and organ of Corti
Cerebellum
Semicircular canals
S.w: The semicircular canals of the inner ear contain the hair-cell receptors that detect rotation of the head. Together with the vestibule they sense balance, and their signals travel on CN VIII.

n.0: The auditory tube equalizes pressure in the middle ear; it does not sense movement.
n.1: The cochlea and its organ of Corti detect sound for hearing, not head rotation.
n.2: The cerebellum uses balance signals to coordinate movement and posture, but it has no receptors; rotation is detected in the semicircular canals.

S.q: A physiology handout lists several ways substances cross cell membranes. Which of these processes require the cell to spend ATP? Select all that apply.
o: Neutrophil engulfing a bacterium
Glucose entering by GLUT carriers
Carbon dioxide leaving a cell
Sodium-potassium pump moving ions
Pancreatic cell secreting an enzyme
Water crossing through aquaporins
S.w: Active transport (the Na⁺/K⁺ pump), endocytosis (phagocytosis by a neutrophil) and exocytosis (enzyme secretion) all use ATP. Diffusion, facilitated diffusion and osmosis are passive.

n.1: Glucose moving down its gradient through GLUT carriers is facilitated diffusion, which needs no ATP.
n.2: CO₂ leaves by simple diffusion down its concentration gradient, with no ATP.
n.5: Water crossing through aquaporins is osmosis, a passive process.

S.q: A hospital places a patient with active tuberculosis in a negative-pressure room and staff wear fitted respirators. Which feature of tuberculosis transmission explains these precautions?
o: TB spreads mainly on objects such as bed rails and doorknobs.
TB bacteria travel in tiny particles that stay suspended in air.
TB is caused by a virus that passes through surgical masks.
TB spreads mainly in large droplets that fall within 2 meters.
S.w: Tuberculosis (bacterium Mycobacterium tuberculosis) is spread by the airborne route: tiny particles stay suspended and travel on air currents, so airflow control and respirators are needed.

n.0: Spread by contaminated objects (fomites) would call for surface cleaning, not special airflow; TB spreads through the air.
n.2: Tuberculosis is caused by a bacterium, not a virus.
n.3: Large droplets that fall within about 1 to 2 meters describe droplet spread, as with influenza; TB is airborne.

S.q: Place these events of the inflammatory response to a contaminated skin wound in order, starting with the first.
o: Mast cells release histamine and other mediators
Phagocytes squeeze out of capillaries and move toward the site
Local blood vessels dilate and capillaries become leakier
Phagocytes engulf and destroy the bacteria
Tissue is injured and bacteria enter the wound
S.w: Injury lets bacteria in. Mast cells (and basophils) release histamine, which causes vasodilation and increased capillary permeability, producing redness, heat, swelling and pain. Phagocytes then leave the capillaries (diapedesis) and follow chemical signals to the site (chemotaxis), where they engulf the invaders (phagocytosis).

S.q: Which type of epithelium lines most of the trachea and bronchi and carries the cilia of the mucociliary escalator?
o: Simple ciliated columnar epithelium
Ciliated simple cuboidal epithelium
Pseudostratified ciliated columnar epithelium
Nonkeratinized stratified squamous epithelium
S.w: The conducting airways are lined by pseudostratified ciliated columnar epithelium with goblet cells: one layer of cells that looks layered, with cilia that sweep mucus upward.

n.0: Simple ciliated columnar epithelium is a true single layer of tall cells that lines the uterine tubes; the trachea and bronchi have the pseudostratified form, whose nuclei sit at different heights.
n.1: Cuboidal cells, some with cilia, line only the smallest bronchioles near the respiratory zone, not the trachea and bronchi.
n.3: Nonkeratinized stratified squamous epithelium resists abrasion in the oropharynx, laryngopharynx and esophagus; it has no cilia and does not line the trachea.

E.q: Read the passage. Select the plural noun that is spelled incorrectly.

parts.t: attornies
memos
criteria

parts: for storing patient records. Charts for patients with confirmed

parts.t: diagnoses
shelves

parts: of the file room, where only authorized staff may open them.

E.w: Attorney ends in a vowel followed by y (-ey), so it simply adds -s: attorneys. Only a consonant followed by y changes to -ies, as in baby and babies.

n.b: Memo is one of the words ending in o that add only -s (memos, photos, pianos). It is spelled correctly.
n.c: Criteria is the standard plural of criterion. It is spelled correctly.
n.d: Diagnosis forms its plural by changing -is to -es: diagnoses. It is spelled correctly.
n.e: Shelf is one of the f words that change to -ves: shelves. It is spelled correctly.

E.q: A wellness flyer reads: "Regular exercise strengthens the heart and lungs. ___, it can improve the quality of a person's sleep." Which transition best completes the flyer?
o: In other words
Conversely
Specifically
In addition
E.w: The second sentence adds another benefit of exercise. "In addition" signals addition.

n.0: "In other words" restates the same idea, but better sleep is a new point, not a restatement.
n.1: "Conversely" signals an opposite idea, but better sleep is another benefit, not an opposite.
n.2: "Specifically" narrows the previous idea, but sleep quality is not a detail of heart and lung strength.

E.q: Read the sentence: "The nurse who works nights trained the student whom we hired." How many dependent clauses does it contain?
o: Three
Zero
Two
One
E.w: There are two relative clauses, each with its own subject and verb: "who works nights" and "whom we hired". The independent clause is "The nurse trained the student".

n.0: "The nurse trained the student" is the independent clause, so it is not counted.
n.1: Clauses beginning with relative pronouns (who, whom) are dependent clauses.
n.3: Both "who works nights" and "whom we hired" are dependent clauses, not just one.

E.q: A nurse is charting a change in a patient's plan, using "however" to link two independent clauses. Which sentence is punctuated correctly?
o: The patient felt better, however, the doctor ordered one more test.
The patient felt better; however the doctor ordered one more test.
The patient felt better; however, the doctor ordered one more test.
The patient felt better however, the doctor ordered one more test.
E.w: When a conjunctive adverb such as "however" joins two independent clauses, use a semicolon before it and a comma after it.

n.0: Commas on both sides of "however" leave two independent clauses joined by commas, a comma splice.
n.1: The comma after "however" is missing.
n.3: With no punctuation before "however", the two independent clauses run together.

E.q: A complete blood count reports the number of erythrocytes in a sample, along with other values. Based on its word parts, what are erythrocytes?
o: Clot-forming cells
White blood cells
Skin pigment cells
Red blood cells
E.w: erythr/o means red and -cyte means cell, so erythrocytes are red blood cells.

n.0: Clot-forming cells are thrombocytes (thromb/o = clot).
n.1: White blood cells are leukocytes (leuk/o = white).
n.2: Pigment cells are melanocytes (melan/o = black).

E.q: Which pair of words correctly completes the sentence? "The school's ____ explained that honesty is a basic ____ of the honor code."
o: principal; principal
principal; principle
principle; principle
principle; principal
E.w: "Principal" names the head of a school (or means "main"); "principle" is a rule or belief, as in a principle of the honor code.

n.0: A basic rule of a code is a "principle", not a "principal".
n.2: The head of a school is the "principal", not a "principle".
n.3: Both words are reversed: the school's head is the principal, and a rule is a principle.

E.q: In Carmen's formal outline, a main point is labeled I. and its first supporting idea is labeled A. How should she label a specific detail that supports idea A?
o: II.
B.
a.
E.w: A formal outline moves from broad to specific as I., A., 1., a. A detail supporting a capital-letter point therefore takes an Arabic numeral: 1.

n.0: II. marks the next main point at the highest level of the outline.
n.1: B. would mark a second supporting idea at the same level as A., not a detail beneath A.
n.3: Lowercase a. is the next level down, used for a detail under a numbered point such as 1.

E.q: A patient is writing to a hospital billing office to dispute a charge. Which sentence best meets the purpose and the audience?
o: Please remove the $85 charge for the March 4 visit, which my insurer paid.
I am writing to you about some issues I have had lately with things on my bill.
Your careless office billed me $85 for March 4, though my insurer paid it.
Hey, quick thing: that $85 charge from March 4 should go, since insurance paid.
E.w: A dispute letter should be courteous and specific: name the charge, the date and the requested action.

n.1: The sentence is polite but vague; it never says which charge is wrong or what should happen.
n.2: The facts are specific, but calling the office "careless" is accusing and likely to make the reader defensive.
n.3: The facts are specific, but "Hey, quick thing" is too casual for a letter to a billing office.

E.q: A student is writing a report on handwashing habits in a school cafeteria. Place the steps in the order the student should complete them, starting with the first.
o: Submit the final copy
Revise the draft's content and organization
Edit the draft for grammar and punctuation
Organize the ideas into an outline
Write a first draft from the outline
Brainstorm a list of ideas about the topic
E.w: Brainstorming and then outlining are both prewriting (generate ideas, then organize them). Drafting turns the outline into paragraphs. Revising fixes the big picture, editing then fixes sentence-level errors, and publishing (submitting the final copy) comes last.

E.q: Read the sentence from a patient's visit summary: "When Dr. Okafor met with Mr. Hale, he explained the test results." Which revision removes the unclear pronoun reference?
o: When Dr. Okafor met with Mr. Hale, they explained the new test results.
Dr. Okafor met with Mr. Hale, and he explained all of the new test results.
When Dr. Okafor met with Mr. Hale, he carefully explained the test results.
When Dr. Okafor met with Mr. Hale, the doctor explained the test results.
E.w: A pronoun must point to one clear antecedent. Replacing "he" with "the doctor" shows that Dr. Okafor explained the results.

n.0: "They" is still unclear (both men? someone else?) and does not identify who explained the results.
n.1: Joining the clauses with "and" keeps the same ambiguous "he" with two possible antecedents.
n.2: Adding "carefully" does not fix the problem: "he" could still mean either man.

E.q: Read the sentence from a shift report: "The charge nurse divided the six patients between Tomas and I so that each of us had three." Which revision corrects the pronoun error?
o: Change "had" to "have."
Change "I" to "me."
Change "us" to "we."
Change "I" to "myself."
E.w: "Between" is a preposition, so both of its objects take the objective case: "between Tomas and me."

n.0: "Each" is singular, so "had" (or "has") is right; "have" adds a tense shift and does not fix "between Tomas and I."
n.2: "Us" is correct as the object of the preposition "of"; "each of we" would create a new error.
n.3: "Myself" needs an antecedent in the sentence that refers to the same person; the object of "between" needs "me."

E.q: Read the sentence: "The patient seemed anxious before surgery." What part of speech is "anxious" in this sentence?
o: Adjective modifying "patient"
Noun acting as a subject complement
Adverb modifying "seemed"
Verb completing "seemed"
E.w: "Seemed" is a linking verb, so the word after it describes the subject: "anxious" is a predicate adjective describing "patient".

n.1: "Anxious" describes the patient rather than naming something; a noun complement would rename the subject (for example, "seemed a calm patient").
n.2: After a linking verb the describing word modifies the subject (a noun), so it is an adjective; the adverb form would be "anxiously".
n.3: The whole verb is "seemed"; "anxious" is not a verb form, so it cannot complete the verb.

E.q: Read the sentence from a discharge summary: "After reviewing the lab results, a new medication was ordered." Which revision corrects the dangling modifier?
o: After reviewing the lab results, the doctor's decision was to order a new medication.
After reviewing the lab results, the doctor's order called for a new medication.
After reviewing the lab results, a new medication was ordered by the doctor.
After reviewing the lab results, the doctor ordered a new medication.
E.w: The person who reviewed the results (the doctor) must be the subject right after the introductory phrase.

n.0: The subject after the comma is "decision," and a decision cannot review lab results; "doctor's" is only a possessive.
n.1: The subject after the comma is "order," so the sentence says the order reviewed the results; the doctor must be the subject.
n.2: The subject after the comma is still "a new medication," so the sentence still says the medication reviewed the results.

E.q: Jasmine is sending a quick text message to a close friend to confirm their lunch plans for today. Which message best fits this audience and purpose?
o: Please be advised that I will attend our scheduled lunch at noon.
Sounds good! See you at noon at the taco place.
Maybe lunch sometime this week? Let me know what works for you.
I am writing to confirm that I will meet you for lunch at noon today.
E.w: Register should match the audience. A text to a close friend is informal: short, friendly and conversational.

n.0: "Please be advised" is a formal business phrase that sounds cold in a message to a friend.
n.2: The casual tone fits, but the message fails the purpose: it does not confirm today's lunch plans.
n.3: "I am writing to confirm" is formal letter language, too stiff for a quick text to a close friend.

E.q: Read the orientation notice. Select the sentence that contains a punctuation error.

parts.t: Please bring the following items to orientation: a photo ID, your vaccination record, and a pen.
The skills lab closes early on Fridays; plan to finish your practice by 3 p.m.
Students who miss orientation must reschedule; however, open spots are limited.
Each new student's supply kit includes: gauze, tape, and gloves.
Clinical sites are in three cities: Austin, Texas; Tulsa, Oklahoma; and Reno, Nevada.

sn.a: Please bring the following items to orientation: a photo ID, your vaccination record, and a pen.
sn.b: The skills lab closes early on Fridays; plan to finish your practice by 3 p.m.
sn.c: Students who miss orientation must reschedule; however, open spots are limited.
sn.d: Each new student's supply kit includes: gauze, tape, and gloves.
sn.e: Clinical sites are in three cities: Austin, Texas; Tulsa, Oklahoma; and Reno, Nevada.

E.w: A colon must follow a complete independent clause. "Each new student's supply kit includes" is not complete, because the verb includes still needs its object, so no colon belongs there: "includes gauze, tape, and gloves."

n.a: The words before the colon form a complete clause, so the colon correctly introduces the list.
n.b: The semicolon joins two independent clauses; the second is a command with the understood subject you.
n.c: A semicolon before the conjunctive adverb however, with a comma after it, correctly joins two independent clauses.
n.e: The colon follows a complete clause, and semicolons correctly separate list items that already contain commas.

E.q: Original sentence: "Frequent handwashing is the single most effective way to stop the spread of infection in hospitals." Which version, with a citation added, is an acceptable paraphrase?
o: Frequent handwashing is the most effective way to stop infection from spreading in hospitals.
In hospitals, the best way to keep infections from spreading is for staff to wash their hands often.
Frequent hand cleaning is the single most useful way to halt the spread of infection in hospitals.
Hospitals should place handwashing stations in every patient room to cut infection rates.
E.w: An acceptable paraphrase keeps the original meaning but uses the writer's own words and sentence structure. This version reorders the sentence (starting with the setting) and rewords it while keeping the same idea.

n.0: This keeps almost all of the original wording and structure, which is patchwriting, a form of plagiarism even with a citation.
n.2: Swapping a few synonyms into the original sentence structure is still patchwriting.
n.3: This adds a new recommendation the original never made, so it does not restate the source's idea.

E.q: During chemotherapy, a patient's blood test revealed leukopenia, so the nurse reviewed infection precautions with him. Based on its word parts, what does leukopenia mean?
o: A deficiency of white blood cells
A cancer of the white blood cells
An excess of white blood cells
A deficiency of red blood cells
E.w: leuk/o means white and -penia means deficiency, so leukopenia is a shortage of white blood cells (which explains the infection precautions).

n.1: Cancer would be shown by carcin/o or -oma (or -emia in leukemia, a blood condition); -penia means deficiency.
n.2: An excess would use hyper- or -cytosis; -penia means deficiency.
n.3: Red is erythr/o; leuk/o means white.

E.q: A soccer player was kicked in the thigh, and by the next day a firm, painful hematoma had formed under the skin. Based on its word parts, what is a hematoma?
o: A shortage of blood cells
A swelling or mass of blood
An inflamed blood vessel
A tumor of the liver
E.w: hemat/o means blood and -oma means a tumor or mass, so a hematoma is a localized mass (swelling) of blood, such as a deep bruise.

n.0: A shortage of cells would use -penia (or anemia, a blood condition); -oma means a mass.
n.2: Inflammation of a vessel would use vas/o or angi/o with -itis.
n.3: Liver is hepat/o, the look-alike root; hemat/o means blood.

E.q: A travel nurse lists the cities on her contract schedule. Which sentence is punctuated correctly?
o: The tour stops in Boise; Idaho, Reno; Nevada, and Provo; Utah.
The tour stops in: Boise, Idaho; Reno, Nevada; and Provo, Utah.
The tour stops in Boise, Idaho; Reno, Nevada; and Provo, Utah.
The tour stops in Boise, Idaho, Reno, Nevada, and Provo, Utah.
E.w: When series items already contain commas (city, state), semicolons separate the items so each pair stays together.

n.0: The semicolons are placed inside each pair instead of between the pairs.
n.1: A colon must not follow a preposition such as "in".
n.3: With commas only, the reader cannot tell where one city-state pair ends and the next begins.

E.q: A staff memo describes a charge nurse in several ways. Which sentence contains an appositive phrase?
o: Ms. Lee, the charge nurse, approved the schedule.
Ms. Lee, approving the schedule, thanked the charge nurse.
Ms. Lee approved the schedule for the charge nurse.
Ms. Lee, who is the charge nurse, approved the schedule.
E.w: An appositive phrase is a noun phrase that renames the noun beside it: "the charge nurse" renames Ms. Lee.

n.1: "Approving the schedule" is a participial phrase.
n.2: "For the charge nurse" is a prepositional phrase.
n.3: "Who is the charge nurse" has a subject and a verb, so it is a relative (dependent) clause, not a phrase.

E.q: To track her walking program, the physical therapist asked an adult patient to wear a pedometer on her waistband all week. Based on its word parts and the context, what does a pedometer most likely measure?
o: Steps taken on foot
Body heat during a walk
Growth in a child's height
Heart rate during exercise
E.w: ped can mean foot or child, and the context (an adult's walking program) points to foot. A -meter measures, so a pedometer counts steps taken on foot.

n.1: Body heat would involve therm (heat), as in thermometer.
n.2: ped can mean child, but the patient is an adult tracking her walking, so foot is the meaning here.
n.3: Heart rate would involve cardi/o (heart), which is not in the word.

E.q: Read the sentence from a quality report: "Since the new reminder policy started, the clinic has saw fewer missed appointments." Which revision corrects the verb error?
o: Change "has saw" to "seen."
Change "has saw" to "have seen."
Change "has saw" to "has seen."
Change "has saw" to "had saw."
E.w: Two steps: "since" calls for the present perfect, and a singular subject ("clinic") takes "has" + the past participle "seen."

n.0: A past participle cannot stand alone as the main verb; it needs "has."
n.1: "Seen" is right, but "clinic" is singular, so the helping verb must stay "has."
n.3: "Saw" is the simple past and cannot follow any helping verb; the participle is "seen."

E.q: Read the paragraph. (1) The nurse asked, "Have you eaten today?" (2) The patient said that he wasn't hungry. (3) She wondered why he had skipped breakfast? (4) Later, she wrote "poor appetite" in his chart. Which sentence contains an end-punctuation error?
o: Sentence 1
Sentence 2
Sentence 3
Sentence 4
E.w: Sentence 3 is an indirect question (she wondered why ...), which is a statement and ends with a period, not a question mark.

n.0: Sentence 1 correctly places the question mark inside the quotation, because the quoted words are a question.
n.1: Sentence 2 is an indirect quotation, correctly ending with a period.
n.3: Sentence 4 is a statement ending with a period after the quoted phrase.

E.q: A pharmacy newsletter is printing a short problem-and-solution paragraph. Place the sentences in the order that creates the most logical paragraph, starting with the first sentence.
o: Many patients forget to take their evening medications.
Another option is a phone alarm set for the same time each night.
Together, these tools can help patients stay on schedule.
One simple solution is a weekly pill organizer with a labeled slot for each day.
E.w: The paragraph states the problem first, then gives solutions: "One simple solution" introduces the first, "Another option" adds the second, and "Together" sums up both tools. "These tools" must follow the sentences that name them.

E.q: A nursing student is writing about a short poem in a class essay that follows US conventions. Which sentence is punctuated correctly?
o: Her favorite poem is "Night Shift at Mercy."
Her favorite poem is Night Shift at Mercy.
Her favorite poem is 'Night Shift at Mercy.'
Her favorite poem is "Night Shift at Mercy".
E.w: The title of a short work such as a poem goes in quotation marks, and in US style the period goes inside the closing quotation mark.

n.1: The title of a short work such as a poem must be enclosed in quotation marks.
n.2: US style uses double quotation marks; single marks are for a quotation within a quotation.
n.3: Placing the period outside the closing quotation mark is British style, not US style.

E.q: A pharmacy newsletter describes the work of a pharmacist and her intern. Which of the following is a simple sentence?
o: The pharmacist counted the pills while her intern labeled them.
The pharmacist and her intern counted, sorted, and labeled the pills.
The pharmacist counted the pills, and her intern labeled them.
After the pharmacist counted the pills, the intern labeled them, and they left.
E.w: A simple sentence has exactly one independent clause. A compound subject (pharmacist and intern) and a series of verbs (counted, sorted, and labeled) still form one clause.

n.0: "While her intern labeled them" is a dependent clause, so the sentence is complex.
n.2: Two independent clauses joined by ", and" make a compound sentence.
n.3: Two independent clauses plus the dependent clause "After the pharmacist counted the pills" make it compound-complex.

E.q: A student is summarizing a small pilot study in a formal paper: "The results ___ that patients who walked daily recovered faster." Which word is most accurate and appropriate?
o: confirm
prove
suggest
establish
E.w: Two checks: the word must be formal, and it must match the strength of the evidence. A small pilot study "suggests" a result.

n.0: "Confirm" presents the finding as verified, which one small pilot study cannot do.
n.1: One small pilot study cannot prove a conclusion; "prove" overstates the evidence.
n.3: "Establish" claims the finding is settled, which overstates what a small study shows.

E.q: While revising, Malik notices that his conclusion introduces a new statistic about hospital costs that appears nowhere else in his essay. What is the best revision?
o: Move the statistic to a body paragraph and restate the thesis instead
Add two more statistics so the conclusion fully develops the point
Keep the statistic so the essay ends with its strongest new evidence
Change the statistic into a question to leave readers thinking
E.w: A conclusion restates the thesis in new words and sums up; it should not introduce new evidence. Evidence belongs in a body paragraph that supports the related point.

n.1: Adding more new evidence makes the problem worse by turning the conclusion into another body paragraph.
n.2: New evidence in the conclusion is undeveloped and breaks the conclusion's job of wrapping up.
n.3: Rewording the statistic as a question still introduces new material in the conclusion and leaves the evidence unsupported.

E.q: Lucia is writing a personal statement for a nursing program's admissions committee. Which sentences are appropriate for this audience and purpose? Select all that apply.
o: My long-term goal is to work as a pediatric nurse in a rural clinic.
Nursing has been my dream for years, and I am super excited to start!
Without a doubt, I will be the strongest student your program has admitted.
Caring for my grandmother after her stroke showed me what skilled nursing looks like.
Volunteering at a hospice taught me to listen before I act.
E.w: A personal statement may use first person, but it must stay formal and purposeful. The correct sentences give specific experiences and goals in standard language.

n.1: The intensifier "super" and the exclamation point are too casual for an admissions committee, and the sentence gives no specific experience.
n.2: The boastful, unsupported claim is arrogant and does not suit a formal personal statement.

E.q: An editor is checking adverbs formed by adding -ly in a discharge leaflet for patients. Which adverb is spelled correctly?
o: finaly
gentlely
carefuly
publicly
E.w: "Publicly" is formed by adding -ly straight to public; it is the standard exception to the -ically pattern.

n.0: Final + ly keeps both l's: "finally".
n.1: Adjectives ending in -le replace the e with y: gentle becomes "gently".
n.2: Careful + ly keeps both l's: "carefully".

E.q: A medical terminology instructor asks students to work out the meaning of in- from context. In which sentence does the prefix in- mean "not"?
o: The tumor was found to be inoperable.
The nurse will inject the vaccine into the upper arm.
Patients should inhale slowly through the mouth.
Insert the catheter gently into the opening.
E.w: in- can mean not or into. In inoperable it means not: the tumor is not able to be operated on.

n.1: In inject, in- means into: to throw (ject) medicine into the body.
n.2: In inhale, in- means into: to breathe in.
n.3: In insert, in- means into: to put something into an opening.

E.q: As part of a rehabilitation assessment after a stroke, the occupational therapist tested the patient's manual dexterity. Based on its root, which body part does manual dexterity involve?
o: The feet
The voice
The hands
The eyes
E.w: The root man/manu means hand, so manual dexterity is skill in using the hands.

n.0: Foot is the meaning of ped/pod (as in podiatrist).
n.1: Voice is the meaning of voc/vok (as in vocal).
n.3: Eye or sight comes from vis/vid or ocul/o, not manu.

E.q: A community college brochure describes a nursing pathway program. Which sentence uses "not only...but also" correctly?
o: The program not only trains nurses but also it places them in local clinics.
The program trains not only nurses but also places them in local clinics.
The program not only trains nurses but also places them in local clinics.
Not only does the program train nurses but also places them in local clinics.
E.w: Correlative pairs must be followed by matching elements. Here each part is followed by a verb phrase: "not only trains ... but also places."

n.0: "But also" is followed by a full clause ("it places"), while "not only" is followed by a verb; the two parts do not match.
n.1: "Not only" precedes a noun ("nurses") but "but also" precedes a verb ("places"); each part needs the same form.
n.3: "Not only" introduces an inverted clause, but "but also" introduces a bare verb phrase, so the pair is not parallel.

E.q: A patient education sheet describes a medication's results. Which sentence uses "affect" and "effect" correctly?
o: The new medication did not affect her sleep, but it had an affect on her appetite.
The new medication did not effect her sleep, but it had an effect on her appetite.
The new medication did not effect her sleep, but it had an affect on her appetite.
The new medication did not affect her sleep, but it had an effect on her appetite.
E.w: "Affect" is usually a verb meaning "to influence" (did not affect her sleep); "effect" is usually a noun meaning "result" (an effect on her appetite).

n.0: After the article "an", the noun meaning "result" is needed: "effect".
n.1: "Did not ___ her sleep" needs the verb meaning "influence", which is "affect"; "effect" as a verb means "bring about".
n.2: Both are reversed: the verb should be "affect" and the noun should be "effect".

E.q: Read the sentence: "Smiling at the child, the nurse gave the injection." What is "Smiling at the child"?
o: A participial phrase modifying "nurse"
A gerund phrase acting as the subject
A dependent clause modifying "gave"
An infinitive phrase showing purpose
E.w: "Smiling at the child" is an -ing verbal phrase that describes the nurse, so it is a participial phrase acting as an adjective.

n.1: The subject of the sentence is "the nurse"; the phrase describes the subject rather than acting as it.
n.2: A clause needs a subject and a verb; this phrase has no subject.
n.3: An infinitive phrase begins with "to".

E.q: A student's paragraph argues that hospitals should serve healthier food in their cafeterias. Which sentence would best conclude the paragraph?
o: Some hospitals currently serve meals from national fast-food chains in their lobbies.
First, cafeterias should add more fresh vegetables and whole grains to each meal.
Hospital parking fees are another issue that deserves attention from administrators.
Healthier menus would let hospitals model the habits they urge patients to adopt.
E.w: A strong concluding sentence restates or extends the paragraph's main point without adding a new topic.

n.0: This sentence is a supporting detail, not a conclusion that wraps up the argument.
n.1: "First" signals the start of a list of supporting points, which belongs in the body of the paragraph.
n.2: This sentence introduces a new topic (parking) instead of closing the argument about food.

E.q: Noah is writing a report on flu vaccine safety for his health class. Which source would be the most credible for his report?
o: A CDC web page on vaccine safety updated this year
A federal fact sheet on flu vaccines published in 2009
A health magazine article quoting two family doctors
A vaccine maker's web page summarizing its own trials
E.w: A credible source is current, written by experts, and free of a conflict of interest. The CDC page meets all three tests; the 2009 fact sheet is outdated, the maker's page is biased, and the magazine article is a secondhand report for general readers.

n.1: It comes from an expert agency, but a 2009 fact sheet is out of date for a report on flu vaccines, which are reformulated every season.
n.2: A popular magazine article is a secondhand account written for general readers; the agency that monitors vaccine safety is a more authoritative source.
n.3: The manufacturer profits from the vaccine, so its summary of its own trials has a conflict of interest.
